correctness.rationale: PASS. Each full transformation decomposes uniquely into a permutation of s cyclic vertices with exact order p and n−s labeled rooted forest vertices of maximal depth h. Ordered distance-layer parent assignments give E_(n−s,s,h); Möbius inversion of permutation orders gives Q_(s,p). A monogenic embedded submonoid has φ(p) generating maps at h=0 or1, unique generator for h≥2; these preserve s. Thus the joint quotient C(n,s)Q_(s,p)E_(n−s,s,h)/c(h,p) is exact, including m=0 and p=1. Counting the h≤1 overcounts produces M_n=n^n−∑_s C(n,s)(s!−C_s)s^(n−s), with bound n exp(1/2−n/3) for relative error. Independent enumeration of all functions n=1..5 produced total embedded counts 1,4,26,237,2842 and checked nonzero triple classes (1,3,7,14,26); finite sample does not prove all degrees.

The joint maximal-depth, eventual-cycle-period and stable-rank distribution is an exact natural embedding statistic for finite transformation dynamics; knowing h,p alone does not recover the distribution of the eventual image size s. The prior total and asymptotic, and the elementary generator lemma, add no value here; ranking this as a modest finite combinatorial refinement rather than a new global monoid classification.
